title: Horn of plenty: why Scotland's national animal has never existed

sents.en: Most countries choose an eagle, a lion or a bear as their emblem; Scotland settled on a beast from legend.
sents.zh: 大多数国家选老鹰、狮子或熊作为国家象征；苏格兰却选定了一头传说中的神兽。

sents.en: Centuries later, it shows no inclination to trade it in for something more plausible.
sents.zh: 几百年过去了，苏格兰丝毫没有想把它换成一个更“靠谱”的动物的意思。

sents.en: Visitors to Edinburgh soon notice that the city is teeming with unicorns.
sents.zh: 来爱丁堡的游客很快就会发现，城里到处都是独角兽。

sents.en: They rear up on fountains, perch on old market crosses and stare down from the gates of royal palaces.
sents.zh: 它们在喷泉上扬起前蹄，蹲踞在古老的集市十字碑顶上，从王宫大门上俯视众人。

sents.en: Gift shops, naturally, are crammed with plush versions sporting rainbow manes.
sents.zh: 礼品店里自然也塞满了顶着彩虹鬃毛的毛绒独角兽。

sents.en: Few tourists realise that the creature is not a whimsical marketing ploy but Scotland's official national animal.
sents.zh: 很少有游客意识到，这种动物不是什么异想天开的营销花招，而是苏格兰正式的国兽。

sents.en: Medieval Europeans took the unicorn rather more seriously than we do.
sents.zh: 中世纪的欧洲人对独角兽要认真得多。

sents.en: Bestiaries described it as fierce, proud and all but impossible to capture, an apt symbol for a small kingdom wary of its larger neighbour.
sents.zh: 动物寓言集把它描写成凶猛、高傲、几乎不可能被捕获的动物，正好象征一个对强大邻国处处提防的小王国。

sents.en: Its horn was believed to neutralise poison, and so-called unicorn horns fetched extraordinary prices at royal courts.
sents.zh: 人们相信它的角能解毒，所谓的“独角兽角”在各国王室宫廷里能卖出惊人的高价。

sents.en: Most, it later emerged, were narwhal tusks hawked by enterprising traders from the far north.
sents.zh: 后来才知道，大部分其实是一角鲸的长牙，由来自遥远北方、头脑灵活的商人兜售。

sents.en: Scottish kings adopted the beast with enthusiasm, even minting gold coins known as unicorns.
sents.zh: 苏格兰国王们热情地采用了这头神兽，甚至铸造了名叫“独角兽”的金币。

sents.en: When James VI of Scotland inherited the English throne in 1603, the royal coat of arms had to accommodate both nations.
sents.zh: 1603 年，苏格兰的詹姆斯六世继承了英格兰王位，王室纹章不得不同时容纳两个国家。

sents.en: England's lion and Scotland's unicorn were duly placed on either side of the shield, where they remain to this day.
sents.zh: 于是，英格兰的狮子和苏格兰的独角兽被分别放在盾牌两侧，一直保留到今天。

sents.en: In the version used north of the border, the unicorn takes pride of place.
sents.zh: 在苏格兰使用的版本里，独角兽占据了最显眼的位置。

sents.en: Look closely, however, and the unicorn is almost always bound in chains.
sents.zh: 可是仔细看，你会发现那只独角兽几乎总是被锁链捆着。

sents.en: Historians are divided over why.
sents.zh: 历史学家对其中的原因看法不一。

sents.en: An old nursery rhyme, in which the lion and the unicorn brawl over the crown, hints at a rivalry that has never quite subsided.
sents.zh: 有一首古老的童谣，讲狮子和独角兽为争夺王冠大打出手，暗示着一场从未真正平息的较量。

sents.en: Today the unicorn has been co-opted by everyone from toymakers to tech investors, who use the word for start-ups valued at more than a billion dollars.
sents.zh: 如今，从玩具商到科技投资人，人人都把独角兽拿来为己所用；投资人用这个词指估值超过十亿美元的初创公司。

sents.en: Scots regard this craze with a certain amusement.
sents.zh: 苏格兰人看待这股热潮，多少带着点好笑。

sents.en: Their unicorn, they point out, is not a sparkly pony but a belligerent beast with a horn like a lance.
sents.zh: 他们指出，他们的独角兽可不是亮晶晶的小马，而是一头好斗的猛兽，头上的角像一杆长矛。

sents.en: A nation that has spent centuries championing an animal nobody has ever seen can hardly be accused of lacking imagination.
sents.zh: 一个几百年来一直推崇一种谁也没见过的动物的国家，总不能说它缺乏想象力吧。

sents.en: And unlike eagles and bears, unicorns will never go extinct.
sents.zh: 而且和老鹰、熊不一样，独角兽永远不会灭绝。
